Challenges and Considerations The project faced significant hurdles, primarily from Aniak’s remote location and compounded supply chain disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. While global supply chains have largely stabilized, remote regions remain vulnerable to similar disruptions. To account for such risks, future projects in off-road communities could further enhance contingency planning with more flexible timelines and additional logistical allowances—above what is already considered necessary. Budgeting additional time for material procurement and enhanced vendor coordination could mitigate the effects of supply chain disruptions. Implementing these mitigation strategies depends on sufficient project budgets and timelines, which were limited in this case, and budget constraints restricted the scope of the Tribal Office retrofits. Nonetheless, the measurable improvements from the retrofits suggest potential for broader impact. NVA is encouraged to pursue additional funding to extend these benefits to other priority facilities identified in the original audits, such as the Community Center, Duplex, and AVCP Office. Community Impact and Long-Term Energy Performance Energy savings and operational stability can be continued through energy consumption and performance monitoring. Regular monitoring allows for timely identification and correction of any emerging inefficiencies or maintenance issues, thus protecting and potentially enhancing energy savings over the long term. Moreover, targeted training for local maintenance staff on newly installed energy-efficient systems and broader energy management practices should be provided. This training could equip personnel with essential knowledge and skills, thereby maintaining and potentially increasing efficiency gains and fostering long-term community resilience and self-reliance in energy management. Continued monitoring of energy performance metrics at the whole-building level is advised to maintain energy savings and identify further efficiency opportunities in NVA’s building portfolio. Routine training for local maintenance staff on newly installed systems and energy efficient operating practices could help sustain efficiency gains and promote long-term stability.
